html:
The Zuni are a Pueblo people of the Zuni River valley in western New Mexico. Shiwinna is their name for their homeland. Their language is an isolate, not related to any other.

In 1492 they lived in six towns of stone and adobe, farming maize, beans and squash with careful water use, and making fine pottery and turquoise jewellery. They descend from the Ancestral Puebloans.

Their towns were the "Seven Cities of Cíbola" that the Spanish hoped were rich in gold. In 1539 the African explorer Estevanico reached the town of Hawikuh and was killed there. In 1540 Coronado took Hawikuh by force and found no gold. The Zuni joined the Pueblo Revolt of 1680 and took refuge on the mesa of Dowa Yalanne. Afterwards they gathered into one town, Zuni Pueblo, where they still live. See also Zuni and their neighbours the Hopi.
